# max :: rv_soybeans_state_2026_09_07

**Q:** what is the situation on soybeans now? how is it looking 3 months from now?

**TL;DR.** Reading the data as of 2026-09-16, the soybean balance tilts modestly toward higher prices over the next three months: the US stocks-to-use buffer sits at 10.72% [N33], past the line the desk calls tight and falling three marketing years running, and the crush is bidding hard at 2.6 USD/bu [N36]  --  but a record-high harvested area of 34.76 M ha [N42] and an export pace in the 6th percentile of its own record [N29] are the offsetting legs, and the export leg is the one that can flip the read. Fund length is already at 234,920 contracts [N24], the 100th percentile of its own three-year record [N26], so the marginal buyer is thinner than the tight-stocks story alone suggests.

**Why.** ## Mechanism

The physical chain here runs supply -> buffer -> price, and demand -> stocks -> price, and they currently pull against each other.

- **The buffer is thin.** A lower stocks-to-use ratio tightens the balance sheet and points toward higher prices, at high confidence and a zero-to-two-quarter lag. At 10.72% [N33], 23rd percentile of its own ten-marketing-year record [N35], the cushion that absorbs a shock is small. That is what makes the next three months *convex to the upside*: a yield or logistics surprise lands on a thin buffer, while a bumper surprise is capped by the same arithmetic. The skew is right-tailed, not symmetric.
- **The crush is the live demand-pull leg.** Wide crush margins make processors bid aggressively for beans  --  high confidence, zero to one quarter. The board crush reads 2.6 USD/bu, 92nd percentile of its own 250-session record, and is one reading printed under two names (board crush and crush margin), so it is one source of support, not two. Its declared effect window runs 2026-08-20 to 2026-11-20  --  squarely inside the three-month horizon.
- **The loosening legs.** Harvested area of 34.76 M ha [N42], 91st percentile of its own record [N44], loosens supply with a two-to-four-quarter lag, and its window (June to December 2026) is inside the horizon. Weekly export sales at 311.85 thousand MT [N27], 6th percentile [N29] and falling, is a high-confidence channel: a slow pace signals weak demand and loosens the sheet. Note this driver sits one hop upstream of the stocks-to-use ratio  --  a persistently slow pace is what would rebuild that buffer and take the convexity away.
- **Which leg dominates.** The model's price-pressuring supply-glut pattern needs three of its five drivers; only area and the stocks ratio carry readable series here, and two of its legs (Argentine selling incentives, the dollar) have no series this page could read. The price-supportive crush-demand pattern needs two of four and has both readable legs  --  crush margin and board crush  --  at their own tails. On that count, and given the tight buffer, the supportive side is the one I expect to carry the next quarter, with the export pace as the honest caveat.
- **The climate leg is not a live input for this horizon.** One sea-surface reading prints at +1.8 degC [N18], +2.4 sigma on its own ten-year window [N19], and the mechanism model declares it in opposite directions under its two phase names on this market  --  that is two phases of one series, not two conflicting signals. Its price-pressuring phase would loosen South American supply; its effect window on that reading counted from the run's start closed 2026-05-30, and the forward window the desk reads off this print would open 2026-10-31 to 2027-01-31  --  the back edge of the horizon asked about, not the middle of it.

## The record

Observed levels, each as of its own read date:

- US ending stocks for MY2026/27 at 310 Million Bushels [N3], against 325 Million Bushels for MY2025/26 [N14], read 2026-09-11; production 4,535 Million Bushels [N5] and the USDA season-average farm price projection 12 $/bu [N4]  --  that price is a USDA projection for a marketing year not yet settled, not a market print.
- Crop condition 58 pct of acreage rated good-to-excellent [N6], read 2026-09-06. The harvest-progress read returned nothing at all at this as-of  --  the record carries no figure for that scope, and none should be assumed.
- The March 2027 delivery of CBOT soybeans settled at 1,328 US cents/bushel [N2], read 2026-09-14; that is one delivery month, not "the price," and no front-month level is served for this market. The World Bank benchmark reads 482 USD/mt [N15], -0.45533 sigma on its five-year window [N16], read 2026-08-01.
- Two stocks-to-use lookups on the PSD tables returned no records at this as-of  --  not yet published  --  so the only ratio on this page is the one cited above.
- **Dated price response, an older episode.** Across the 2009/10 to 2010/11 marketing years the settled USDA season-average farm price rose from $9.59/bu [N61] to $11.30/bu [N62]. That is a survey-based marketing-year actual, not a futures settle and not a forecast, and it is history, not a template.
- **Dated cascade, the January-April 2025 firing window.** Over that window, CBOT soybeans' May 2025 delivery settle changed -3.1828 % [N63] while ZCE rapeseed meal's May 2025 delivery changed +2.5362 % [N64]; the declared competing-demand relation between those two markets sat at odds with the moves on that firing, read on each board's own-currency move (US dollars and Chinese yuan), with the exchange-rate move inside that comparison, not removed from it  --  the yuan-per-dollar rate moved +0.3201 % [N65] over the same window. Against ZCE rapeseed oil, the May 2025 delivery changed +10.0615 % [N66]; that competing-demand relation also sat at odds with the moves on this firing, again read in each board's own currency with no rate applied. The crush leg behaved as declared: CBOT soybean meal's May 2025 delivery changed -6.6432 % [N67] and the declared same-crush relation held; CBOT soybean oil changed +4.0123 % [N68], the declared meal-to-oil relation held; and CME palm oil changed +4.8007 % [N69], where the declared substitution relation to soybean oil also held. Each of those is a pairwise coincidence on one window defined by an unrelated market's episode, in-sample only. The MATIF rapeseed leg cannot be read at all: that window predates that market's own price history  --  a stated limit, not a zero.
- **How far each layer reaches.** The numbers are read as of 2026-09-16, with the newest knowledge date on a number row 20260904 and the oldest 2026-05-31; the newest dated document behind this page is 2026-04-06; and no per-contract price tape is carried on this page, so there is no session-level tape layer to quote.
- Supporting dated text, all older than the numbers and dated as such: China imposed an additional 10 percent tariff on US soybeans effective 2025-03-10 [E23]; the 2021/22 US outlook was for lower supplies, lower exports, higher crush and higher ending stocks [E18]; and Argentina announced a third special soybean export exchange rate in April 2023 [E28].

## What to watch

Four things, each with the reading that would show it wrong:

- **The stocks-to-use buffer** [N33]  --  past the tight line with three consecutive marketing years falling. This reads wrong if the next print turns back inside that line or the falling run breaks; that is what removes the upside convexity.
- **The crush margin** [N36]  --  top decile of its own record, window open 2026-08-20 to 2026-11-20. Reads wrong if the next print returns the series to the middle of its own record, which takes the count under the demand-pull pattern's own threshold of two.
- **Export sales pace** [N27]  --  bottom decile of its own record, window 2026-08-27 to 2026-11-27. This is the leg that can flip the whole read: it sits one hop upstream of the stocks ratio, so a pace that stays behind rebuilds the buffer rather than drawing it.
- **Harvested area** [N42]  --  top decile. Reads wrong if the next print returns the series to the middle of its own record; until then it is the standing price-pressuring counterweight.

One caution on positioning rather than fundamentals: managed money is at 234,920 contracts [N24], 100th percentile of its own record [N26] and rising three weeks running. That is what the reporting funds held, not a cause the mechanism model declares, but it does mean a supportive balance sheet is already partly owned.

The scheduled publication dates for these series were named once in the data and are not watch items of their own.

**Cascade / convergence**
